Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing fatigue, swelling in your lower legs, and weight loss; could you tell me how long you have been noticing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 66-year-old white male. The patient reports a 10-day history of fatigue and bilateral lower leg swelling. He mentions a weight loss of 3.6 kg (8 lbs) over the past 6 months without trying. He has a history of chronic bronchitis and uses an albuterol inhaler as needed.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fatigue. I also have Lower leg swelling, Unintentional weight loss.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Chronic bronchitis. Social history: History of smoking one pack of cigarettes daily for 44 years and drinks one alcoholic beverage daily.

speaker: Patient
text: The patient denies any recent cough, change in urinary habits, chest pain, dyspnea, or fevers. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That previous suggestion of pneumonia seems unlikely given you explicitly deny cough, chest pain, or shortness of breath. To clarify your history and investigate the causes of your fatigue and weight loss, have you noticed any changes in your thirst, urination frequency, or appetite?

REQUEST TEST: Lipid_Panel
REQUEST TEST: Erythrocyte_Sedimentation_Rate

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Lipid Panel: Total cholesterol 475 mg/dL; Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
The lipid panel reveals severe hypercholesterolemia with a total cholesterol of 475 mg/dL, while your ESR is normal. This combination of fatigue, weight loss, lower leg swelling, and high cholesterol makes familial hypercholesterolemia or a potential liver or cardiac issue more likely than the pneumonia previously suggested. Have you noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes, or any abdominal discomfort?

REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Tests
REQUEST TEST: Lipoprotein_A

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Liver_Function_Tests: NORMAL READINGS; Lipoprotein_A: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal liver function tests and Lipoprotein A make familial hypercholesterolemia and liver failure less likely. Have you noticed any specific skin rashes, such as orange or yellow discoloration on your palms, or any tenderness behind your knees or in your elbows?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis
REQUEST TEST: Anti-HCV, Anti-HIV

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Blood Negative, Glucose Negative, Protein 4+, WBC 0–1/hpf, Fatty casts Numerous; Anti-HCV, Anti-HIV: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Nephrotic Syndrome. The presence of 4+ proteinuria, fatty casts, and concurrent hypercholesterolemia is diagnostic of nephrotic syndrome, likely secondary to a glomerular disease. Given your weight loss and fatigue, please confirm if you have noticed frothy urine or any recent infections, but the clinical picture is now clear.
